ABSTRACT Staphyloccus aureus responds to environmental changes in part by adjusting proteome levels through selective proteolysis.
TrfA plays a role in regulating the proteome by controlling the abundance of proteins involved in stress responses, competence, and antitoxins.

TrfA, like the adaptor MecA, plays a key role in the selective degradation of a subset of proteins, including proteins involved in the response to stress, the regulation of virulence factors, and the regulation of the proteolytic system.
